definitions.gloss: seven spring herbs; seven herbs of spring
definitions.explanation: A set of seven edible wild herbs traditionally eaten in a rice porridge on January 7th. The seven herbs are: seri (water dropwort), nazuna (shepherd's purse), gogyo (cudweed), hakobera (chickweed), hotokenoza (henbit), suzuna (turnip), and suzushiro (daikon radish).

examples.japanese: {一月|いちがつ}{七日|なのか}に{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat the seven spring herbs on January 7th.

examples.japanese: スーパーで{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}のセットを{買|か}ってきた。
examples.english: I bought a set of seven spring herbs at the supermarket.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}の{食|た}べ{過|す}ぎで{疲|つか}れた{胃|い}を{休|やす}めるために、{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}を{入|い}れた{七草粥|ななくさがゆ}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made seven-herb porridge with the spring herbs to rest my stomach, which was tired from overeating during New Year's.

notes:
A deeply rooted New Year tradition in Japan. On January 7th ({人日|じんじつ}の{節句|せっく}), families prepare {七草粥|ななくさがゆ} (seven-herb rice porridge) using these seven herbs. The custom is believed to ward off illness, bring good fortune for the year, and give the stomach a rest after rich New Year foods.

THE SEVEN HERBS:
- {芹|せり}: water dropwort
- {薺|なずな}: shepherd's purse
- {御形|ごぎょう}: cudweed
- {繁縷|はこべら}: chickweed
- {仏の座|ほとけのざ}: henbit
- {菘|すずな}: turnip
- {蘿蔔|すずしろ}: daikon radish

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {七草粥|ななくさがゆ}: seven-herb rice porridge
- {七草|ななくさ}セット: seven-herb set (sold at supermarkets in early January)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Supermarkets across Japan sell pre-packaged sets of the seven herbs every January. There is also {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven autumn herbs), but those are traditionally for viewing, not eating.
